experiments.question: Is the first header word the insertion position or the text length?

trials.operation: typed three lines, caret at end, Escape

F10 Corkboard from DOS, type A then B at 52-53, Left x3, Escape, exit, DEBUG read

trials.operation: reopen the 64-byte note, Shift+Left x7, Escape
trials.note: both journals contain modifier and arrow keys only; probe-select also pressed Down once and is not the published seven-step trial

trials.operation: save 2794-byte note with caret at 42, cold reopen

experiments.result: word0 is the caret byte offset in the text area at the moment the note was written; when that offset lands on a CR the row-boundary convention is unresolved
experiments.confidence: strong: T3 separates position from length, T4 separates close-time from edit-time capture; T5 and T6 survive only as final files

experiments.question: Does a close rewrite the note when only the caret moved?

trials.note: reopen then Home; identity was observed at the time but the before-image was not kept

trials.interval: cold reopen, Home, Escape, quit, extract

counter_observations.evidence: the word 51 comes from T4's in-session DEBUG read; T5's journals send no text key; the retained final file is the only surviving bytes
captures b01/b02 and the final rsx-b extract; the pre-trial file was not retained

experiments.result: a plain cursor-only close on a freshly opened note left the file unchanged in T2 and T7b; T5 and T6 moved the caret and left a changed word, so a general no-write rule is not established
experiments.confidence: strong only for T7b's whole-file comparison; T5 and T6 cannot be adjudicated from retained evidence
experiments.unresolved: whether a selection, or a reopen in the same boot after an edit, marks the buffer dirty

experiments.question: What is the second header word?
experiments.result: unestablished; zero in every measured state
experiments.confidence: the exclusions are strong for the states exercised; the meaning is unknown

experiments.question: What is the real editable capacity, as distinct from the 2860-byte text area?

trials.refusal: the CR that would begin row 66
the CR that would begin row 66
trials.note: characters continued onto row 65 after the refused CR
no 42-character cap observed on the first row of an empty note

trials.composition: 65 rows, append to the last row

trials.post_refusal_control: Home still moved the caret; the close stored word0 from it

units.visual_row: a drawn row; a longer logical line wraps over several

experiments.result: the editor accepted 65 drawn rows of 42 characters in these CR-delimited compositions; 2794 bytes is the largest stored text demonstrated, not a proven universal maximum
experiments.confidence: strong for the trials and this edition at 640x480; wrapped-line compositions were not driven to refusal, so other arrangements are unmeasured
limits: C3 accepted 81 characters on one logical line, so 42 is a wrap width, not a line-length cap
no trial filled the row budget with wrapped lines, so the byte maximum for that shape is unknown

experiments.question: Is the text area ASCII or CP437?

trials.operation: open a seeded note containing CP437 high bytes
trials.observed: the editor drew the CP437 glyphs for 82 9B B0 B1 B2 C4 C9 CD DB E1 F1

trials.operation: Alt+130 and Alt+225 on the numeric keypad, then Escape

experiments.result: the text area holds CP437 bytes; the editor renders them and preserves them across a save
experiments.confidence: strong at two nonadjacent typed code points; the rest of the high half is inferred from display and preservation only, so the reader's 0x20-0xFF acceptance is policy rather than measurement
